newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.18 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.18 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.18 percent to close at 1.0276 per greenback in seesaw trade on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
Banks continued speculating over dollar outflows, dealers said. Over the last five sessions, net dollar flows registered a total deficit of $222.1 million.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Tuesday deficit of $65 million.
But some dealers said some financial transactions have not yet been registered, which could push net dollar flows into surplus.

They also said another reason for the real's gain was that some banks decided to sell dollars to take advantage of the dollar's recent gain in value due to dollar outflows. The sales increased the supply of dollars in the market, improving the value of the real.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real ended at 1.0314 per dollar, up 0.02 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real dropped 0.46 percent to close at 1.095 real per greenback.
